history.p: According to the diary of the Norwegian composer Halfdan Kjerulf, Gade wrote two movements for his fourth symphony during Christmas 1849. On 22 March 1850, it was already finished, so that he could bring it with him to Leipzig in June, where he handed it over to his publisher Friedrich Kistner. Whereas the first three symphonies had had their first performances in Leipzig, the fourth symphony was premiered by the newly founded Orchestra of Musikforeningen (The Music Society) of which Gade had been appointed conductor. The symphony became extremely popular all over Europe. In Germany it was the most performed contemporary symphony during the second half of the 19th century.
